name: Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA)

header.one_liner: India's national design authority for combat aircraft, under the Department of Defence R&D; designed the LCA Tejas and now leads the ₹15,000-crore Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme plus Tejas Mk-2 and TEDBF, executing through public-private industry partnership.

what_it_is.prose: The Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA) is India's national design and development authority for combat aircraft, established in Bengaluru in 1984 under the Department of Defence Research & Development (DDR&D) of the Ministry of Defence as an autonomous society and DRDO affiliate. ADA was created to manage the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) programme and is the design house behind the HAL Tejas — India's first indigenous fourth-generation fighter — with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited as the production agency and the National Flight Test Centre (NFTC), run under ADA, conducting flight testing. ADA does not manufacture aircraft; it owns the design, systems integration, flight-control law development, testing and certification-support work. Beyond the in-service Tejas Mk-1/Mk-1A, ADA is executing three successor programmes: the more powerful Tejas Mk-2 (medium-weight fighter), the Twin Engine Deck-Based Fighter (TEDBF) for naval carrier operations, and the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) — India's fifth-generation stealth fighter, with a development-phase outlay of about ₹15,000 crore. On 27 May 2025 the Raksha Mantri approved the AMCA Programme Execution Model, under which ADA leads the programme and executes it through industry partnership offering equal, competitive opportunity to both private and public sector firms (independently, as joint ventures or as consortia), with an Expression of Interest to follow. Dr Jitendra Jaisingh Jadhav has been Director General since 11 September 2024, and DRDO leadership has publicly framed the near-term roadmap as delivering Tejas Mk-2 followed by AMCA as the Tejas programme passes its 25-year mark.

deployments_procurement.summary: ADA's 'deployments' are its aircraft programmes rather than direct procurement contracts. Its delivered product — the Tejas — is in Indian Air Force service and in serial production at HAL (Tejas Mk-1A order tranche). Its pipeline is the Tejas Mk-2, TEDBF and the fifth-generation AMCA, the last now cleared for execution through a competitive public-private industry-partnership model approved by the Defence Minister in May 2025.

open_questions: AMCA prototype rollout and first-flight dates are not yet firmly fixed in public MoD statements
Selection of AMCA industry-partnership winner(s) had not been announced as of the verification date
Engine path for AMCA (GE F414 interim vs future 110-130 kN co-developed engine) is not finalised publicly

import_dependencies.summary: ADA's airframe design, flight-control laws, mission-systems architecture and integration are indigenous, but the platforms it designs depend on imported propulsion and several sensor/avionics elements. Tejas Mk-1/Mk-1A and Mk-2 use US GE engines (F404 / F414), and AMCA's initial engine is expected to be the GE F414 pending an indigenous high-thrust engine. AESA radar, EW suites and some seekers involve foreign technology or co-development.

Future AMCA engine subject to foreign co-development discussions (Safran/GE/RR); not yet secured

faq.question: What is ADA and how does it relate to HAL and DRDO?
faq.answer: The Aeronautical Development Agency is India's national design authority for combat aircraft, set up in Bengaluru in 1984 under the Department of Defence R&D and affiliated to DRDO. ADA owns the design, systems integration, flight-control development and flight testing (via the National Flight Test Centre) of India's fighters, while Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) is the production agency that manufactures them. ADA designed the Tejas; HAL builds it.

faq.question: What is ADA's role in the AMCA fifth-generation fighter?
faq.answer: ADA leads the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme, India's fifth-generation stealth fighter, with a development-phase outlay of about ₹15,000 crore. On 27 May 2025 the Defence Minister approved the AMCA Programme Execution Model under which ADA executes the programme through industry partnership, giving private and public sector firms equal opportunity on a competitive basis — bidding independently, as joint ventures or as consortia — with an Expression of Interest to follow.

faq.question: What aircraft programmes is ADA running besides AMCA?
faq.answer: Alongside the in-service Tejas Mk-1/Mk-1A, ADA is developing the Tejas Mk-2 (a more powerful medium-weight fighter powered by the GE F414 engine, targeted for delivery within roughly four years per DRDO statements) and the Twin Engine Deck-Based Fighter (TEDBF) for naval carrier operations, in addition to the AMCA. A persistent gap across all of these is indigenous propulsion, since India has yet to field a certified indigenous fighter engine.
